_why: The Requests merge, step 2. GET /signing-requests/v2 returns one row per
signing, and TWO screens declared what that row contains — the agenda at
/signings declared fourteen fields, and the merged tracker declared
eleven. Nothing compared them, so nothing objected.
The three the tracker was missing were `live`, `days_waiting` and
`stale`: exactly the fields CANCEL1 and DASH1 added so that a screen
would stop deciding for itself which signings are over and which have
gone quiet. A screen that does not declare them cannot render them, so
the merged tracker showed cancelled and expired signings mixed in with
live ones and could not mark a single stuck request — the signal the
agenda's whole design leads with.
This is FLOW1 item 0's defect one endpoint over, and milder only by
luck: there the names were WRONG and rendered as undefined, here they
were ABSENT and rendered as nothing at all. Both are one contract
declared twice in two languages with no referee between them.
This file is the referee, in the shape shared_deed_row_keys.json and
phone_cases.json already use: one list, read from both sides, so drift
costs two deliberate edits instead of one silent omission. The backend
asserts its emitted key set equals this by EQUALITY; the frontend suite
asserts the SigningSummary interface declares exactly these fields.
EQUALITY, not containment, in both directions. A subset check passes a
screen that quietly drops a field — which is precisely the failure this
file was written for.
